subject: Post-call: Finlytics eval plan, model recommendations & rollback options
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hogan <alex.hogan@finlytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Finlytics eval plan, model recommendations & rollback options

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single plan: 

What we heard
- Primary use case: real-time sentiment + issue classification in analyst workflows (avg. prompt length ~220 tokens, latency target <350ms p95).
- Current blocker: recent model update at your side caused a subtle drop in sentiment precision on edge cases (financial sarcasm / compound negation).
- Success metrics for pilot: precision >= 88% on the bank-specific eval set, p95 latency <350ms, cost goal <= $0.004/token.

Our recommended experimental plan
1) Evaluation artifacts (we attached): curated prompt_sets_finlytics_v1.json and a short eval harness.
2) Model recommendations: start with redwood-gpt-2.7b-int8 for latency-sensitive endpoints, and redwood-gpt-7b-q8 for your highest-quality batch jobs.
3) Pinning/rollback: we propose pinning the real-time route to model version redwood-gpt-2.7b-int8@v2026-03-12 while we run comparative diffs. If that passes, we can enable auto-rollforward.
4) Canary & metrics: 10% traffic canary with the new variant, run the regression diff script (regression_diff_scan_20260319.md) across the 1k edge-case prompts.

Next steps / owners
- Alex/Priya: confirm which route you want canaried (real-time vs. batch) — reply by EOD Tue.
- Marissa: I’ve copied the eval harness and will spin up a job to compare v2026-03-12 vs latest. Target results by Friday.
- Ben/Rishi: please prepare a rollback checklist and an SLA exception note if we need to revert at scale.

Attachments: finlytics-eval-summary-20260320.pdf, prompt_sets_finlytics_v1.json, regression_diff_scan_20260319.md

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
From: Alex Hogan <alex.hogan@finlytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finlytics eval plan, model recommendations & rollback options

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications: 
1) When you say 'pin to v2026-03-12' — will that affect our historical logs or just the serving route? We need to ensure auditability for compliance.
2) Are the attached prompt sets representative of the full 1k edge-case sample or a smaller slice?

We’d like to canary the real-time route first (that’s where customers saw the change). Priya and I can confirm by 17:00 PT.

— Alex
Director, Product — Finlytics
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hogan <alex.hogan@finlytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finlytics eval plan, model recommendations & rollback options

Alex — great questions. Short answers:

- Pinning semantics: pinning a route in Redwood binds the serving route to a model artifact version for inference only; logs and historical tokens remain untouched and are tagged with the active model id at time of request for audit purposes. We’ll provide a short audit doc snippet for your compliance team.

- Prompt set coverage: prompt_sets_finlytics_v1.json is the curated 200-edge-case slice we discussed. We’ll run the full 1k in the diff job; the attachment is intentionally smaller to speed local review.

Action: we’ll kick the canary on the real-time route if you confirm. Marissa will post preliminary diff metrics to the shared Drive link. Rishi/Ben will attach rollback checklist by 15:00 PT.

On Tue, Mar 17, 2026 at 09:00 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Slotted in a quick rollback runbook below — high level:
> - Step 1: Pause canary traffic.
> - Step 2: Re-pin route to redwood-gpt-2.7b-int8@v2026-03-12.
> - Step 3: Lift throttles incrementally and monitor error/latency metrics.
> - Step 4: Post-mortem + fix plan.
>
> I’ll attach a more detailed checklist (including required DocuSign for SLA exceptions) in the thread.
>
> — Rishi

Cheers,
Vanessa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finlytics eval plan, model recommendations & rollback options

Quick internal update for the thread before we push the canary live: 
- Marissa: I started the comparative run against the 1k set. Initial sniff shows a 3.2% hit on precision for the new variant vs pinned v2026-03-12 on the sarcasm subset — need full run to confirm.
- Rishi: see attached regression_diff_scan_20260319.md for the failing prompt ids; please validate rollback checklist items 2 and 4 (re-pin + traffic ramp).
- Vanessa: after Alex confirms, I’ll schedule the canary at 20:00 PT and keep the window to 2 hours with automatic rollback if precision delta > 2% or latency p95 increases > 70ms.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
